title: Great God, How Infinite Art Thou
description: Great God, How Infinite Art Thou in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 67, headed “God's eternal dominion”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Great God, how in-fin-ite art thou! What worth-less worms are we! Let the whole race of crea-tures bow And pay their praise to thee.

lines: Great God, how infinite art thou!
What worthless worms are we!
Let the whole race of creatures bow
And pay their praise to thee.
Thy throne eternal ages stood,
Ere seas or stars were made;
Thou art the ever-living God
Were all the nations dead.
Nature and time quite naked lie
To thine immense survey,
From the formation of the sky
To the great burning day.
Eternity with all its years
Stands present in thy view;
To thee there's nothing old appears,
Great God, there's nothing new.
Our lives thro' various scenes are drawn,
And vex'd with trifling cares;
While thine eternal thought moves on
Thine undisturb'd affairs.
Great God, how infinite art thou!
What worthless worms are we!
Let the whole race of creatures bow
And pay their praise to thee.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
